problems: The blind guess (a human stick figure with a raised arm and legs apart) does not match The Bridled Kite. The drawing reads as a thin skeletal line figure, not a kite with a sail, pennant, ribbons and tail.
Apex 77257 (~310,213) and right shoulder 77070 (~320,232) are nearly on top of each other, so the sail has no readable upper-right edge and no sail shape.
The sail is not a closed silhouette. Only a sliver between apex, left corner 77622 (~287,271) and the shoulder is visible, so it does not read as a sail.
Tassels 77660 (~285,425) and 77516 (~293,431) overlap into one knot instead of forming a fork at the foot of the tail.

Labels collide badly: 'bend in the right-hand streamer' overlaps 'far tip of the right-hand streamer', and the apex, shoulder, and tassel labels are stacked on top of each other, so the stars cannot be matched to their parts.
Gold lines dominate and the blue lines run as a second, nearly parallel path. The figure looks like a traced copy of the connection lines rather than a filled silhouette of the kite.
output.advice: Redraw as a filled kite silhouette, upright, with the pennant pointing up and the tail hanging down. Keep the stars where they are, except for these changes. (1) Separate apex 77257 (~310,213) from right shoulder 77070: move the shoulder out to roughly (350,250) on the upper-right edge so the sail is a clear diamond from apex (310,213) to shoulder (350,250) to left corner 77622 (287,271), closed back up to apex. (2) Keep pennant tip 76276 at ~(367,148) connected to the apex by a single straight spar. (3) Keep left ribbon 80179 (~129,341) and tip 80883 (~84,321) as a smooth curved streamer off the left corner. (4) Keep right streamer bend 75761 (~398,324) and tip 74975 (~447,326), but move the tip label so it no longer overlaps the bend label. (5) Spread the tassels: put left tassel 77660 at about (270,430) and right tassel 77516 at about (312,440), both fed from the foot of the tail below the left corner, so they form a visible fork. (6) Fill the sail and tail with a solid silhouette, and draw the gold lines as thin outlines only, so the figure reads as a kite and not as a stick skeleton. (7) Offset the labels so none overlap, with leader lines to each star."]
